I can still help you push for a refund directly with the plumber. Here’s a simple plan:

1) Collect evidence
- Photos: Take clear photos of the leak reappearing and the visible damage around the pipe (close‑ups and a wider shot).
- Timeline: Write down dates/times: when they came, what they did, when the leak started again, and any follow‑up attempts.
- Paperwork: Keep the invoice, quote, and any texts/emails with them.

2) Contact the company (or individual)
Use email or text so you have everything in writing. You can say something like:

“On or around [exact date if you know it], I hired you to repair a leak at [address]. The leak returned the next day, and there is visible damage around the pipe you worked on (photos attached).  
Because the work was unsatisfactory and caused additional damage, I’m requesting a full refund of [amount] and a written plan to repair the damage at no additional cost.  
Please respond within 5 business days so we can resolve this amicably.”

3) Escalate if needed
If they refuse or ignore you:
- Check if they’re licensed: Your state’s contractor or plumbing license board often accepts complaints.
- Payment method:
  - Credit card: File a dispute/chargeback citing defective service and damage.
  - Debit/ACH: Ask your bank about a dispute for services not rendered as agreed.
  - Payment apps (PayPal, etc.): Open a “significantly not as described” or similar dispute with your evidence.
- Reviews/complaints: As a last resort, you can file complaints with the Better Business Bureau or post factual reviews (sticking to verifiable details).

If you’d like, tell me:
- The business name,
- How you paid (card/cash/app),
- The amount you paid,

and I’ll draft a tailored message you can send to request a full refund and repair of the damage.</action>
